space.adverse_direction: ON means the exposure's next-day return is LOWER than on OFF days; the direction is part of each claim and is never searched both ways

candidates.mechanism: An inverted curve has preceded recessions because short rates exceed long rates only when markets expect growth to fall, and equity earnings fall with growth.
The three month version of the inversion reads the policy stance more directly, and a restrictive stance lowers equity returns by tightening financing.
A widening credit spread means lenders demand more for default risk, which has led falls in equities that depend on the same borrowers.
A credit spread above its own recent median marks a regime in which risk is being priced higher, and equities carry less cushion in it.
Rising implied volatility marks rising demand for protection, and volatility clusters, so adverse days come in runs after a rise.
A rising real yield raises the rate at which future earnings are discounted, which lowers equity valuations when it moves quickly.
A strengthening dollar tightens global financial conditions and lowers the dollar value of foreign earnings of the companies in the index.
The credit premium is the compensation for default risk, and a widening spread is the market repricing that risk against the position.
A spread above its own recent median means the compensation is being repriced upward, and the repricing hurts the long credit leg first.
An inverted curve signals expected recession, in which default risk rises and corporate bonds underperform Treasuries of the same duration.
Rising equity volatility marks risk aversion across markets, and investors sell corporate bonds against Treasuries during risk aversion.
The product is short volatility, so a rising volatility index is the adverse state itself and volatility clustering says it persists.
Credit stress usually precedes or accompanies volatility spikes, so widening spreads may warn before the short volatility position is hurt.
A rapidly strengthening dollar is a global funding stress channel, and funding stress is a recurring cause of volatility spikes.

decisions.by: Oscar Carmenate Rodriguez, Director del Proyecto
decisions.consequence: The rule can only be harder, so it rescues no denied hypothesis and loosens no gate. The cost is that it unblocks nothing on its own: the screen serves to choose better monitors. Sealed as a governance record before any scan; see artifacts/governance/monitor-screen-link-rule.json.
decisions.decision: OPTION C. A link confirmed by the screen is an ADDITIONAL requirement for a premium that relies on it: the premium must pass R3 under M1 on its own measurement window AND the screen link. The screen link never replaces M1.

exposures.name: variance risk premium via the VIX futures roll

fixed_parameters.why_fixed: declared here, not searched: tuning either would multiply the candidates and turn a screen into a fit
fixed_parameters.why_history: the 21 day change needs 22 observations and the 252 day median needs 253 before a state can be read, so each series is loaded from this date; history before the window is a level and never a return

holdout_rule.applies_to: only candidates that pass the discovery rule, and only once
holdout_rule.claim: on the holdout, the mean next-day exposure return on ON days minus OFF days has an upper 95 percent bound below zero
holdout_rule.test: moving-block bootstrap, seed 0, block 5, 2000 resamples, confidence 0.95, the same parameters as every other bound in the engine
holdout_rule.why_not_the_fold_rule: three years cannot hold five usable folds, so the holdout uses one pooled claim, declared here and not chosen after seeing the discovery result

space.justification: Four monitor links have been measured on this project and three were refuted (VIX minus realised volatility on XYLD 4 of 6 and QYLD 3 of 7, the VIX term structure on SVXY 2 of 5). Each refutation cost a full declare, capture, measure and seal cycle. A scan over a sealed list costs minutes and counts every candidate, so a variable is only built around once it has led adverse returns on a window it was selected on AND on a holdout the scan could not read. Passing the scan is NOT evidence that a premium pays: it only says the variable is worth declaring a monitor on.

multiplicity.note: Prior tests are counted, not rescanned: a screen that forgot the four it already ran would be reporting one candidate in nineteen as one in fourteen.

pass_rule.source: the engine's own M1 constants (premium_engine.LINK_MINIMUM_USABLE_FOLDS and LINK_CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD, monitors.MINIMUM_TRIGGER_DAYS_PER_FOLD). Nothing is set here, so the screen cannot be easier or harder than the gate a premium will later face.
pass_rule.what_it_tests: a fold counts when the mean next-day return of the exposure on days the state is ON is below its mean on the days it is OFF; a fold with fewer than 10 ON days is unusable, not failed

space.purpose: Find which candidate monitor variables lead adverse returns of a premium exposure, BEFORE any premium is declared around them. Every premium measured so far was declared with its monitor and the monitor then failed R3; this inverts the order.
space.return_definition: next-day close-to-close return, adjusted for distributions, of the exposure held long; for the credit pair, the next-day spread return of long LQD against short IEF

state_forms.ABOVE_TRAILING_MEDIAN_252: the series is above its own median of the previous 252 trading days (no threshold chosen)
state_forms.CHANGE_21D_ABOVE_ZERO: the series is higher than 21 trading days earlier (sign of a fixed-horizon change, no threshold)
state_forms.SIGN_AT_OR_BELOW_ZERO: a published difference is at or below zero (the only parameter-free boundary)
